name: Greedy
tagline: Take the best move now, once you know it never hurts later.
signals: split into as many parts as possible
template:
def can_reach_end(A):
    reach = 0                      # farthest index reachable so far
    for i, step in enumerate(A):
        if i > reach:              # stuck before i
            return False
        reach = max(reach, i + step)
    return True

print(can_reach_end([2, 3, 1, 1, 4]), can_reach_end([3, 2, 1, 0, 4]))  # -> True False
complexity: Usually O(N), or O(N log N) with a sort

blocks.html:
Paying with the fewest coins: take the biggest coin that fits, then repeat. Greedy makes the best-looking move at each step and never goes back.

It is fast, but only correct when you can say why the local choice is safe.

blocks.text: Example: where to start a road trip

blocks.note: Try every start, then one pass that skips starts that cannot work

blocks.html: Greedy is safe only with a reason. Here: if you run dry at i, every start between start and i runs dry there too, so you skip them all in one step.

blocks.q: Coins 1, 3 and 4, amount 6. Does taking the biggest coin first give the fewest coins?
options: No: 4 + 1 + 1 is three coins, 3 + 3 is two
Only if the coins are sorted
blocks.why: A greedy rule needs a reason it never hurts. Without one, test a small counterexample; if it fails, reach for dynamic programming.

pitfalls: Greedy without a reason is a guess. Try a small counterexample before you commit.
Sort by the right key: to fit the most non-overlapping intervals, sort by end, not start.
Check the global condition first (total gas against total cost), so the single pass can trust its answer.
